extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders submitting comments on EPA's proposed perchlorate National Primary Drinking Water Regulation (public water systems, States, Tribes, water sectors, industry, NGOs, scientists, and other interested members of the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and specific topics for public comments on EPA's proposed National Primary Drinking Water Regulation for perchlorate, including statutory benefit-cost determinations, proposed MCL/MCLG levels, monitoring, treatment, occurrence, and various statutory and executive-order analyses. Intended to direct evidence, analyses, and data stakeholders should provide during the notice-and-comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit-Cost Determination (SDWA §1412(b)(4)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing an NPDWR, the Administrator must publish a determination whether the benefits of the MCL justify, or do not justify, the costs based on the analysis conducted under SDWA section 1412(b)(3)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluated quantified and nonquantifiable benefits and costs; found monitoring and administrative costs comprise a significant percentage of total costs and that due to low occurrence only few systems would see health benefits, leading to the determination that benefits do not justify costs for the proposed MCLs. EPA requests comment and supporting data on this determination and underlying analysis (see Economic Analysis sections and Exhibits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Statutory Pathway to Set MCL (SDWA §1412(b)(6)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where benefits do not justify costs, the Administrator may promulgate an MCL that maximizes health risk reduction benefits at a cost that is justified by the benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluated higher alternative MCLs (40 µg/L and 80 µg/L) to determine whether benefits could be maximized at reasonable cost; although net benefits increased slightly at higher MCLs (due to fewer systems needing treatment), monitoring/administrative costs remained substantial and net benefits remained negative; EPA seeks comment on whether any MCL could be set under this provision and on supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Submission Expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are most helpful when accompanied by specific examples and supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should provide specific, data-backed evidence, studies, or analyses when addressing any requested topic to improve the Agency's record and support potential regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplification and Burden Reduction Without Reducing Health Protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek ways the proposed NPDWR could be simplified and burden (including paperwork and administrative burden) reduced without affecting the rule's ability to prevent known or anticipated adverse health effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requests concrete suggestions and supporting data on simplifications and burden-reducing options; focus on mechanisms that maintain required health protections while lowering administrative or paperwork costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small System Burden and Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify ways to further reduce burden on small water systems, including potential flexibilities for monitoring and compliance dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is specifically seeking comment on monitoring flexibilities, alternate compliance schedules, and other provisions to lessen impacts on systems serving ≤10,000 people; provide data on costs and feasibility for small systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Date Practicality and Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate practicability of compliance timing, including whether EPA should require compliance sooner than three years after final rule or offer an additional two-year nationwide extension for capital improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requests comments and data on system capacity and timelines for capital improvements to inform practicable compliance dates and potential nationwide extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation Challenges (especially for small systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential implementation challenges associated with the proposed regulation that EPA should consider, particularly for small systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should include specific operational, technical, financial, or administrative challenges and provide evidence or examples to support proposed mitigations or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Risk Characterization and 'Restoring Gold Standard Science' EO
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the consistency of the proposed rule and supporting documents with the Agency's guidelines on risk characterization and Executive Order 14303 (“Restoring Gold Standard Science”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evaluations of how the risk characterization follows Agency guidelines and EO requirements and identify any deviations or areas needing improvement with supporting rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and Rigor of Epidemiological Evidence for MCLG
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the quality and rigor of the scientific review, evaluation, and use of epidemiological studies that investigated associations between maternal thyroid hormone level and neurodevelopmental outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide critiques or supporting analyses of the epidemiology, study selection, causality assessments, and applicability to sensitive populations, including citation of alternative studies or re-analyses where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and Uncertainties of Perchlorate Reference Dose and BBDR Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess adequacy and uncertainties in derivation of the perchlorate reference dose, including the health effects assessment and the biologically based dose-response (BBDR) model inputs and assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA lists model inputs selected to represent a sensitive population: weak TSH feedback loop (pTSH=0.398), low iodine intake (75 μg/d), low baseline maternal fT4 (10th percentile, 6.7 p.m.), and first trimester (13th week). Comments should evaluate the appropriateness of these inputs, provide alternative values or justifications, and address model structure and parameter uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of pTSH Selection and 'Weak' TSH Feedback Characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a 'weak' TSH feedback response is a reasonable characteristic for the sensitive population and whether the applied pTSH value (0.398) is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requests comments on the selection of pTSH=0.398, alternative pTSH values (e.g., 1 to represent median response), and implications for the derived MCLG; provide data, literature, or model runs supporting alternative selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Benchmark Response (BMR) for MCLG Derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the Agency's choice of a 1% BMR for deriving the MCLG is appropriate or whether a 2% or 3% BMR should be used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit analyses showing how different BMR selections change the MCLG and the public health implications of those choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed MCL Levels and Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comment on the three proposed MCLs (20 µg/L, 40 µg/L, 80 µg/L) and any other alternative MCL higher than the MCLG, including data supporting that a given alternative maximizes health risk reduction benefits at a cost justified by benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address whether 20 µg/L is the closest feasible level to the MCLG, whether higher MCLs are more appropriate under SDWA provisions, and provide cost, occurrence, monitoring, and health-benefit evidence for alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on Setting an MCL When Benefits Do Not Justify Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on what MCL, if any, the Agency may appropriately set consistent with the statute where low occurrence means benefits are not justified by costs at any MCL, including when unquantified benefits and uncertainty are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide statutory interpretation, policy arguments, or empirical analyses supporting alternative approaches to identify an appropriate MCL under such circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occurrence Data and Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide additional data sources on perchlorate levels in drinking water and comment on adequacy of assumptions and analyses used to estimate occurrence, including levels below quantified detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requests data, methods, or critiques related to occurrence estimation, including the Perchlorate Occurrence and Monitoring Report and methods for imputing or characterizing non-detects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and Estimate of Systems Likely to Exceed MCL
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the method used and the estimated number of systems likely to exceed the proposed MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical data, alternative modeling, or critiques of EPA's approach to estimating systems exceeding given MCL thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring Framework and Initial Monitoring Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the proposed monitoring framework, compliance schedule, public notification elements, initial monitoring requirement (who must monitor and number of samples), and proposed flexibility for small groundwater systems to collect two samples instead of four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational data or analyses supporting alternative sampling frequencies, sample counts, or monitoring frameworks and assess implications for detection, compliance, and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Historical Data to Satisfy Initial Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on EPA's proposal to allow water systems to use historical data to satisfy initial monitoring requirements, including whether EPA should specify a cut-off date (currently January 1, 2021) or additional conditions for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide recommendations on appropriate cut-off dates, quality assurance for historical data, and circumstances under which historical data should or should not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic Reduction of Monitoring Frequency and Thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate EPA's proposal to allow systems to automatically reduce monitoring frequency without State approval based on initial monitoring results (thresholds e.g., 4.0 µg/L or one-half MCL) and allowable frequencies (annual, triennial, nine-year), and the proposal allowing States to require more frequent monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or modeling showing how thresholds and reduced frequencies affect detection of exceedances and public health protection; propose alternate thresholds or schedules as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Binning Monitoring and Waiver Provisions (40 CFR 141.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposes that after systems are binned into monitoring frequencies based on initial monitoring, systems should follow monitoring frequencies and waiver provisions in 40 CFR 141.23 for IOCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address whether 141.23 procedures are appropriate for perchlorate and suggest modifications or clarifications if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Calculation for MCL Exceedance and Follow-Up Sampling Timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether an exceedance should be based on the average of an initial sample and confirmation sample versus a running annual average, and on the proposed five-day timeframe for a follow-up sample (alternatives include 3 or 10 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational or analytical justification for preferred exceedance calculations and sampling timeframes, including implications for false positives/negatives and treatment response times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notification (PN) Tiering and CCR Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether Tier 1 public notification following a perchlorate MCL exceedance is appropriate or whether Tier 2 PN should be required; comment on accuracy and clarity of mandatory health effects language in appendix A to subpart Q and language describing sources of perchlorate in appendix A to subpart O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggested PN tiering, specific wording edits, or alternative messaging based on risk communication best practices and supporting evidence of comprehension and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment Technologies and WBS Model Assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comment and data on the costs, availability, and effectiveness of treatment technologies and non-treatment options for perchlorate removal, including assumptions in the WBS model and the assumption that systems can design/operate to produce finished water concentrations equal to 80% of the MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA seeks data on capital and O&M costs, technology performance including impact of competing ions on perchlorate-selective resin bed life, and real-world operational constraints; also requests comments on SSCT affordability analyses and income measures used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Additional Treatment Technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data or information on any treatment technologies not identified in EPA's analyses that have been shown to reduce perchlorate to the proposed MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include performance data, pilot/full-scale study results, cost estimates, and operational limitations for novel or less-common technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of Health Risk Reduction Cost Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the adequacy of estimates, assumptions, and analyses used to estimate costs and benefits and to describe unquantified costs and benefits; provide additional data or approaches to quantify unquantified benefits and on unit costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects comments on unit cost assumptions for PWSs and States, cost estimates for small systems, potential omitted costs, and alternative analytic approaches; provide supporting datasets or methods where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on Administrator's Finding that Benefits Do Not Justify Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comment and information on the Administrator's finding that benefits do not justify costs for proposed MCLs (20, 40, 80 µg/L) and on the proposal to adopt one of these MCLs notwithstanding that finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit analyses or data challenging or supporting the finding, including valuation of unquantified benefits and sensitivity/uncertainty analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Approaches to Identify an MCL
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comment on other approaches for identifying an MCL for which benefits justify the costs and on EPA's conclusion that no alternative MCL would 'maximize health risk reduction benefits at a cost that is justified by the benefits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose alternative benefit-cost frameworks, interpretation of statutory requirements, or econometric/occurrence/health benefit approaches that could identify a justifiable MCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (ICR) Burden and Information Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICR summarizes the information collection activities, estimates respondents/affected entities (owners/operators of PWSs and States), frequency, total burden (650,564 hours/year), and total estimated cost ($36,282,282/year). EPA solicits comments on need, accuracy of burden estimates, and methods to minimize respondent burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comments on the necessity of requested data elements, accuracy of respondent counts and burden hours, alternatives to reduce burden, and any suggested changes to the ICR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) Analysis for Small Entities
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA certified the action will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities (small defined as systems serving ≤10,000 persons) and provided estimates of systems that could incur costs exceeding thresholds (e.g., >1% or >3% of revenue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address the accuracy of small-entity impact estimates, revenue estimation methods, thresholds used, and whether additional small-system flexibilities are warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA determined the action does not contain an unfunded mandate of $100 million or more in any one year and assessed potential impacts on small governments; EPA consulted with small governments and invites comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or arguments if commenters believe the action would create an unfunded mandate exceeding statutory thresholds or would significantly/uniquely affect small governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism Considerations and Consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA concluded the action does not have federalism implications but may be of significant interest to State and local governments and consulted with representatives and organizations early in the rule development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and local governments should provide comments on implementation, resources, and state-federal coordination needs; EPA provided a docket summary of consultation input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal Implications and Consultation (EO 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA concluded the proposed rule may have Tribal implications, identified 1,026 Tribal-serving systems potentially subject to the rule, and conducted consultations with Federally recognized Tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribal officials are specifically solicited to provide additional comment; EPA notes capital expenditures for compliance may be eligible for DWSRF funding. Provide Tribal-specific impact data and funding/implementation concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's Health Evaluation (EO 13045)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the action is significant and may disproportionately affect children (e.g., decreased IQ in offspring of iodine-deficient, hypothyroxinemic pregnant women), EPA evaluated effects on children and applied its Policy on Children's Health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address how children's health considerations were incorporated and whether the evaluation and chosen MCL options adequately protect children, with supporting health data or alternative analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy Impacts (EO 13211) Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assessed whether the proposed rule is a 'significant energy action' by evaluating effects on energy supply, distribution, or use and concluded it is not significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or analyses if commenters believe the rule would have significant adverse effects on energy supply, distribution, or use (e.g., additional electrical demand from treatment systems) contrary to EPA's conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Voluntary Consensus Standards and Analytical Methods (NTTAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposes to use voluntary consensus standards for monitoring and analysis where appropriate and proposed five analytical methods (EPA Methods 314.0, 314.1, 314.2, 331.0, 332.0) that include QC criteria for accurate quantitation of perchlorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA invites comments identifying potentially applicable voluntary consensus standards and explaining why they should be used; provide method performance data or recommendations for analytical method selection and QC criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with Advisory Bodies (SAB, NDWAC, HHS)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA consulted with the National Drinking Water Advisory Council, HHS, and the Science Advisory Board; SAB provided input and EPA developed PBPK/BBDR models in collaboration with FDA scientists to address recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments can address whether EPA appropriately considered advisory body recommendations, sufficiency of model development in response to SAB advice, or remaining scientific uncertainties requiring further advisory review.
